# China Nature

> Independent guide to China's natural landscapes — karst, danxia, mountains, lakes, deserts, grasslands, glaciers, forests, wetlands and the Tibetan plateau. Find your perfect destination with the trip finder, comparisons and itineraries. No tour sales.

## Core

- [Home](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/): Ultimate guide to China's nature — trip finder, 10 landform families, destination comparisons, itineraries, wildlife and practical planning advice (visa, tickets, altitude).
- [Travel Guide](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/guides/): The practical companion — what to pack per climate zone, what to eat by region, where to stay at each park gate, how to move around China, a 6-step plan, 10 mistakes to avoid, photography tips and the 14 UNESCO natural sites.
- [FAQ](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/faq/): 21 answers covering visas, seasons, park tickets, altitude, packing, costs, food and safety.
- [About](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/about/): Who we are and our editorial standards — firsthand research, no sponsored listings, sources cited.
- [Contact](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/contact/): Email for corrections, questions and feedback.
- [Privacy Policy](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/privacy/): Privacy-respecting analytics, no personal data collection.
- [Terms of Use](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/terms/): Terms for using the site's content.

## Key Sections

- [Trip Finder](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/#trip-finder): Filter 12 destinations by landscape type, season, difficulty and altitude.
- [Landscapes](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/landscapes/): The 10 landform families of China — karst, danxia, mountains, lakes, deserts, grasslands, glaciers, forests, wetlands, plateau — explained with the best place to see each.
- [Compare](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/#compare): Zhangjiajie vs Guilin vs Jiuzhaigou — the honest answer.
- [Wildlife](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/#wildlife): Giant pandas, snow leopards, golden monkeys, Tibetan antelope and more.
- [Itineraries](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/#itineraries): 5, 7 and 10-day routes through China's nature.
- [Sources](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/#sources): UNESCO and Wikipedia references cited on this site.

## Travel Guide (practical)

- [What to Wear](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/guides/#packing): Packing checklist and clothing per climate zone.
- [What to Eat](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/guides/#food): Regional dishes at each nature destination.
- [Where to Stay](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/guides/#stay): Where to book for each park, with price ranges.
- [Getting Around](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/guides/#transport): High-speed rail, flights, private cars and park shuttles.
- [Plan Your Trip](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/guides/#plan): A six-step planning checklist.
- [Mistakes to Avoid](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/guides/#mistakes): 10 errors that cost travelers a day.
- [Photography](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/guides/#photography): How to shoot the classic frames.
- [UNESCO Sites](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/guides/#unesco): The 14 World Natural Heritage sites of China.
- [When to Go](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/guides/#seasons): Best season per landscape, month-by-month planning and what it costs per day.
- [All 12 Destinations](https://www.chinanaturetrip.com/guides/#cheat-sheet): Seasons, difficulty, altitude, days and entry fees for every destination in one table.

## Destination Guides

- [Guilin & Yangshuo](https://guilin-yang-shuo.com/): Karst peaks, Li River cruises and bamboo rafts.
- [Zhangjiajie National Park](https://zhangjiajie-national-park.com/): The Avatar sandstone pillars.
- [Yunnan Province](https://yunnan-province.com/): Stone Forest, rice terraces and Xishuangbanna.
- [Shangri-La](https://shangri-la-yunnan.com/): Tibetan town at 3,200m in Yunnan.
- [Tibet & Lhasa](https://tibet-lhasa-potala.com/): The Roof of the World.
- [Dunhuang & Jiuquan](https://dunhuang-jiuquan.com/): Silk Road dunes and the Mogao Caves.
- [Dujiangyan Panda Base](https://dujiangyan-panda-base.com/): Giant pandas up close.
